self.raw_excerpt:
Self-review — REQ-3 Phase 2 content round (monorepo).

Scope match: the round walked all 18 requirements against the code and minted
FR-01.17 and FR-01.18. Both mints were operator decisions and are now recorded
in the iterate spec's Spec Impact section, which an external review correctly
found stale.

Correctness of the artifact under change: the catalog is consumed by two
production parsers, the RTM generator and the compliance updater. All were run
against the changed file — 23 catalog-contract tests and 417 integration tests
green, and the RTM regenerated so all 18 requirements keep a resolving deep link.

What I checked myself and found wrong, then fixed:
- Nine ledger rows claimed "tested" on assumption rather than evidence; a
  targeted test search corrected them and left exactly one honestly untested.
- FR-01.16 criterion 5 was inherited unchanged and is untrue (nothing creates
  the target project's domain glossary). Left standing as a carded promise,
  knowingly, and stated as such.
- Five FR-01.05 criteria carried no enforcement classification at all.
- Seven bare prompt-only rows had reappeared after the 2026-07-25 sweep.
- The glossary and the ledger header pointed at superseded/dismissed ids.
- Two triage cards described the same mechanism in different words.

Known and deliberate: two forward-looking criteria in FR-01.16, both carded;
glossary at 527 lines and the elicitation module at 409, both above the round's
own convention and neither gated; FR-01.18 criterion 1 (same repo, same grade)
is enforced by construction but has no test.

Risk: none of this changes runtime behaviour. The executable changes are test
pins extended for the new requirement, and a regenerated compliance artifact.

plan.disposition: Plan review not re-run at finalization: the round's mini-plan was reviewed externally at intake on 2026-07-23 (GPT+Gemini, mode=iterate) and the plan did not change afterwards. The external pass that DID run at finalization is recorded under external_code against the current head, which is the review the constitution's review-cascade rule asks for on a changed diff.

code.disposition: The code-reviewer subagent was not spawned: this session runs under an explicit operator instruction not to invoke subagents. The diff was instead reviewed by the external cascade against the current head (recorded under external_code, GPT returned five findings, all dispositioned) and by the self pass, and every executable line in it is a test pin verified by running the tests it pins. Recorded as not_run rather than claimed, per the rule that a pass which did not run says so with a reason.

doubt.disposition: Adversarial pass is scoped by the constitution to changes touching risky ground - stored-data migrations, concurrency, or anything hard to undo. This round touches none: the executable delta is test-pin extensions plus a regenerated compliance artifact, and every other change is prose in tracked planning documents. Reverting it is a revert.

findings.finding: The specification permits one pending ADD, `FR-01.17 — /shipwright-grade`, after its mint-or-fold decision. This change instead mints an unrelated `FR-01.17 — Independent re-check on the code host` and assigns `/shipwright-grade` the new ID `FR-01.18`. This both adds an unapproved capability and violates the specified next-free ID for the grade requirement.
findings.suggestion: Remove the independent-recheck FR from this iterate (or obtain and record a separate mint decision), and make the approved grade capability `FR-01.17`. Update the ID/count tests accordingly.

findings.finding: AC3 requires a catalog-wide, consumable by-product listing every acceptance criterion not proven by a test, with one row per unproven criterion. No such artifact is added in this diff; the change only adds catalog criteria and documentation/tests. The evidence ledger mentioned in the session log is also not added or updated here.
findings.suggestion: Add the test-completeness/backfill artifact, enumerate every catalog AC and its proof status, and include a concrete work-item row for every unproven AC. Add a mechanical test that validates the artifact covers all live criteria.

findings.finding: The new `C-02` constraint is outside this iterate’s explicitly stated scope: “Quality requirements and constraints (QR-01, C-01) — the round is about functional requirements.” Adding a new constraint is neither required to make the FR catalog complete nor within the approved MODIFY/ADD list.
findings.suggestion: Remove `C-02` from this change and, if it is a real product constraint, propose it through a separately scoped requirement/constraint iterate.

findings.finding: The updated contract test codifies the erroneous 18-row catalog and accepts `FR-01.18`, rather than testing the scope-approved catalog shape. Consequently it will pass when the unauthorized FR-01.17 and misnumbered grade row are present, masking rather than detecting the spec violation.
findings.suggestion: Keep the expected IDs aligned with the approved scope (`FR-01.01` through the approved `FR-01.17`) until a separately approved mint extends the catalog.

findings.finding: The new rigor tests only search for selected prose substrings in the elicitation document. They do not validate the claimed acceptance-round outcome: that criteria have outcome coverage, that two operator-facing scenarios were recorded, that prompt-only claims are represented in the test-backfill output, or that all catalog requirements were actually walked. A document containing the phrases while the method is not followed would still pass.
findings.suggestion: Retain these drift tests, but add artifact-level validation for the required grill traces/evidence ledger and the AC-to-test completeness report, including coverage of every live FR and criterion.  Overall assessment: block. The change fills many criteria, but it omits the required unproven-criteria work list and introduces an unauthorized/misnumbered requirement, while also expanding into an out-of-scope constraint.
